officialDocs.label: How to submit your app (partner program and allowlisting)

verdict.summary: Any Salesloft user can create an OAuth app in their account and test it within their own team in under an hour. For other Salesloft teams to use it, the app has to be allowlisted, which means being accepted into the Salesloft Partner Program, creating a Marketplace listing and passing a technical review that Salesloft says takes up to 2 weeks.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: App creation is self-serve in an existing Salesloft account, and there's a Test Authorization button. The time is our estimate. It assumes you already have a Salesloft seat.

timeToProd.assumes: A multi-tenant agent that reads people, cadences, calls and emails across customer teams, which needs allowlisting; a Client Credentials app for one customer's team is the faster but private-only path.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partner Program application acceptance (no SLA published), then Marketplace listing approval and allowlisting review (up to 2 weeks; the decision is emailed 7–10 days after submission).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The up-to-2-weeks and 7–10 day figures are Salesloft's. The partner-acceptance wait is our estimate, which widens the range.

verdict.cost: No partner or review fee mentioned. You need a Salesloft account to build and test, and front-end integrations ask for sandbox license details in the technical review form.

prerequisites.item: A Salesloft account (a seat on a Salesloft team) to create the OAuth application
prerequisites.why: Apps are created under Your Applications > OAuth Applications in the Salesloft account.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs don't say whether admin rights are needed to create the app.

prerequisites.item: Acceptance into the Salesloft Partner Program
prerequisites.why: Allowlisting (use by other Salesloft instances) runs through the partner portal: the Join form, then an invite email, then the listing and technical review.

prerequisites.item: OAuth (not API keys) for the integration
prerequisites.why: Salesloft says Partner Applications submitted using API Keys will not be approved.

prerequisites.item: A public English privacy policy, a distinctive icon, and test accounts for reviewers
prerequisites.why: These are on the Marketplace submission checklist.

scopeTiers.impact: Works immediately for users on your own Salesloft team. Other teams need the app allowlisted.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Scope strings are from the scopes page. That allowlisting gates other teams is stated, and the same-day timing for your own team is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: Any app used by other Salesloft instances must pass partner acceptance, a Marketplace listing and the allowlisting review against the API Terms, Design and Brand Guidelines.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: accounts:write appears in Salesloft's example token response. people:write and cadences:write are inferred from the naming pattern.

scopeTiers.impact: Salesloft says these grant elevated access to sensitive data and should be requested with extreme caution and only when absolutely necessary. An agent that reads email bodies needs email_contents:read.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: No separate approval process for privileged scopes is documented. Extra review scrutiny is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: An admin enables it for private application use only. It acts with the permissions of the admin who created it and can't be allowlisted, so it's a per-customer path, not a SaaS connect button.

steps.title: Sign in to a Salesloft account
steps.detail: Sign in and open Your Applications > OAuth Applications.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://accounts.salesloft.com/oauth/applications returned a 302 to /sign_in on 2026-10-20. We didn't sign in.

steps.title: Prepare app config
steps.detail: Pick least-privilege scopes (avoid privileged scopes unless essential), a non-Salesloft HTTPS redirect URI, a name and description, and a 1:1 SVG logo.

steps.title: Create the OAuth application
steps.detail: Click Create New, set Application Type (public Frontend Integration or private team app) and Grant Type = Authorization Code. These two fields can't be edited later. Copy the Application Id and Secret.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://accounts.salesloft.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&state=... and exchange the code at POST https://accounts.salesloft.com/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code.

steps.title: Handle refresh with rotation
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 7200 seconds. Each refresh issues a new refresh token and revokes all old ones, so persist it atomically and serialize refreshes per user.

steps.title: Build API calls within the cost budget
steps.detail: Call https://api.salesloft.com/v2/... The budget is 600 cost per minute per team, shared by all integrations on that team. Deep pagination (page > 100) costs extra points, up to 30 for page 501+. Prefer filters and webhooks over deep paging.

steps.title: Apply to the Salesloft Partner Program
steps.detail: Fill out the Join the Salesloft Partner Program form. After acceptance, you get an invite email to create a partner portal account.

steps.title: Draft listing content and technical review answers
steps.detail: Write the tagline, how-it-works and data-flow text, features, permissions, FAQs and privacy policy, plus answers for the Application Technical Review Form (OAuth setup, endpoints and webhooks used, support contact).

steps.title: Build the listing and submit for approval
steps.detail: Upload the tile and listing images and screenshots (at least one showing the product working with Salesloft), request listing approval, and submit the technical review form with reviewer test accounts.

steps.title: Allowlisting review
steps.detail: Salesloft's development team approves or denies (with reasons). The decision is emailed 7–10 days after submission, and the whole process takes up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Go live on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Once the listing and app are both approved, the profile is published and other Salesloft teams can authorize the app.

agentCanDo: Choose least-privilege scopes and avoid privileged ones
Implement the code flow and rotating refresh-token handling
Budget API calls against the 600 cost/min team limit
Draft listing copy, data-flow description and privacy policy
Fill in the technical review form answers
humanMustDo: Hold a Salesloft seat and create the OAuth app
Apply to and get accepted into the Partner Program
Upload listing images and screenshots and request approval
Provide reviewer test accounts and respond to denials

blockers.symptom: Users on other Salesloft teams can't use your app
blockers.cause: The app isn't allowlisted. Allowlisting is what lets an app be used by other Salesloft instances.
blockers.fix: Join the Partner Program, create a Marketplace listing and pass the allowlisting review.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error users see wasn't documented.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with "does not match the redirection URI used in the authorization request"
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri differs from the one registered or from the one sent to /oauth/authorize.
blockers.fix: Send the identical registered URI in both the authorize and token calls.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with invalid_grant after a parallel refresh
blockers.cause: Getting a new refresh token revokes all old ones, so a second concurrent refresh uses a revoked token.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes per user and store the newest refresh token atomically.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The revocation rule is sourced. The invalid_grant symptom is our inference.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 even though your integration makes few calls
blockers.cause: The 600 cost/min limit is per team, not per integration, so other tools on the customer's team share it. Deep pages cost extra.
blockers.fix: Use backoff, avoid page > 100, and use filters or webhooks.

blockers.symptom: Can't change an app from private to public (or switch grant type)
blockers.cause: Application Type and Grant Type can't be edited after creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new app with the right type.

blockers.symptom: Partner submission rejected for using API keys
blockers.cause: Salesloft doesn't approve partner applications that use API keys.
blockers.fix: Switch to the OAuth authorization code flow.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 2 hours (expires_in 7200). The docs don't state a refresh-token lifetime, but refresh tokens rotate and old ones are revoked on each refresh.
The rate limit is a cost budget of 600/min shared at the team level by every integration, so a noisy neighbour on the customer's team can starve your agent.

Salesloft publishes an OpenID Connect discovery document (issuer https://accounts.salesloft.com, /oidc/authorize, /oidc/token) whose advertised scopes are only system:all, external_emails:create and openid. That's separate from the /oauth/ endpoints the API guide uses.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: We fetched the discovery document on 2026-10-20. How the OIDC endpoints relate to partner apps isn't documented.

nuances.text: Customer security teams are likely to scrutinize Salesloft integrations closely: in August 2025, attackers stole OAuth and refresh tokens from Salesloft's own Drift integration and used them to pull Salesforce data. Expect questions on token storage and encryption.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The incident is sourced. The effect on reviews and customer scrutiny is our inference.

nuances.text: Client Credentials apps act with the creating admin's permissions and are private-only, which suits a single customer that wants a headless agent but can't be distributed.
